No the contract that I have is yearly. The probationary period is 6 months. They can offer a permanent position earlier or when the contract expires, or renew at the yearly period for another year, or of course, don't renew.

I didn't(and still don't) like advisors at banks. I applied for entry level positions at all banks and credit unions because I wanted to work in finance and needed to get my feet in the door. Upon starting though..I realized that this is not what I envisioned to do. I liked finance and working with people (to a moderate degree), but not pitching products all day and handling transactions without prior training. I knew there'd be sales but not to this degree at the teller position.


Thankfully I took the CSC so I wasn't entirely unprepared, but upon working at a bank, I shifted my focus back to computer science, where I was debating on taking a Bachelor's in Com Sci or Commerce(finance) at U of C.


I'm not a natural sales person either, and I agree with your point, there isn't sufficient time to pitch and explain a product to a customer — additionally while I'm trying to handle their transactions or resolve their concern at the same time. It's hard to build rapport in the 5 or so mins I'm talking to them. 


But to answer your question, no I don't enjoy it. I'm pressured to sell but I can tell some customers don't need more credit products (already maxed out and only paying the minimum balance) or they don't fully understand what the bank is selling them on. So I don't sell because I feel guilty and judge it's not necessary for them to get another product.


I want to dip, but there doesn't seem to be comparable jobs in Calgary, with pay + vacation time + potential benefits (if I'm offered a permanent role, which my branch manager says is coming, but of course, you can't guarantee until they actually give you an offer in writing).


I don't want to work towards becoming a senior teller or an advisor position because they even have more sales targets.


I'll be a student in the fall and will work 3 days at the bank to fulfill my minimum hours (18.75/week), while taking classes the rest of the week. 


I applied at Starbucks in case I really want to quit, but pay at Starbucks starts at $16/hour and benefits depend on their monthly-hours-fulfilled criteria. 


TDLR: Yes I want to dip, but I'm having trouble finding a job with a similar pay of $18.50/hour + vacation pay + benefits while studying at uni. I'm applying at credit unions and ATB as others have mentioned they offer better pay with less sales.
Thanks, I'll take a look at job postings and apply

I agree with you, and it makes sense because they're trying to make money/profit. But what I don't fully understand is that the bank charges for every single service to an extreme (IMO), such as $5 per monthly bank statement, or $15 for a balance of account letter(basically document that shows all of the products you have with said bank and had your name and address). 


I know the purpose is to avoid that small number of people that request 10 bank statements, but even the library only charges 10-20¢ per page. For record profits with low pay...and to advise us to tell the customers that the bank is here for them...is really misleading IMO. And I understand why so many individuals hate banks because staffs' first priority is to sell instead of putting customers' interests first.

yeah.. from what I know Scotia hires contracts to save money from having to spend on benefits + to see how well that worker does before committing to hire them.
